posts.content: Maximize good-player welfare: cooperate with likely good opponents; defect against reliably selfish opponents. Track actions and update beliefs; communication is unavailable.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect when evidence makes an opponent more likely selfish than good.

Against likely-good players, cooperate to protect shared welfare; defect against likely-selfish players to improve good players’ payoff. Update beliefs from observed actions; no messages are available.
Prioritize total welfare of good players: cooperate with likely-good opponents, and defect when evidence suggests they are selfish or will defect. Update beliefs from observed play.
Prioritize good-player welfare: cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones. C from P3/P6 supports good, while D from P1/P9 raises selfishness suspicion.
Prioritize total welfare among good players: C is best against a good opponent; D can benefit us against a selfish one. Use identity and observed-action evidence to decide.
P5 is unobserved, so use the prior; cooperate unless evidence suggests selfishness.
P8 is unobserved, so use the prior: favor C against a likely-good opponent; D only when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely. Update beliefs from observed play.

Prioritize good-player welfare: cooperate with a likely-good opponent; defect if evidence makes selfishness likely. Update beliefs from observed actions, remembering good players may also defect strategically.
P2 cooperated when we met, supporting a good identity; cooperate again to preserve good-player welfare.

own_previous_reports.strategy: Cooperate with uncertain opponents to support good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and defect against reliably selfish opponents.
Cooperate when the expected welfare among good players is higher; use observed actions to update identity beliefs and defect only when that improves good-player welfare.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to support shared welfare; defect when evidence makes an opponent likely selfish. Update identity beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with the unobserved opponent; prior cooperation is evidence P3 and P6 are good, while P9’s defection raises suspicion. Update beliefs from observed actions and prioritize good-player welfare.
Cooperate with P10 at current uncertainty; observed cooperation from P3 and P6 supports good identities, while defections by P1 and P9 raise suspicion. Prioritize welfare of good players.
Cooperate with an uncertain opponent to support good-player welfare; observed defections raise selfishness estimates, while cooperation supports good identity.

Cooperate with P5: the prior probability they are selfish is below one half, so cooperation better supports good-player welfare. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good role and defections as weaker evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with an unobserved, likely-good opponent to support good-player welfare. Observed defections raise selfishness estimates; observed cooperation lowers them.
Cooperate with P4: absent evidence, cooperation supports good-player welfare. Prior defections raise suspicion about P1, P9, and P10; cooperation from the others supports good identities.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize the sum of cumulative payoffs of ALL actual good players, including yourself, excluding any selfish player. You do not know which other players share this objective.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: Each player writes a private strategy note that only that player sees. Players cannot send messages to one another.
Messages and notes allow at most 96 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Choose your action for the current opponent. Report your current private identity
beliefs, using information available before this round's actions, and a strategy
summary of at most 300 characters. Return action, beliefs, and strategy.
